Visible screen context and your command are sent to the AI provider you configure. That provider handles data under its own terms.

Explicit preference memory saves only what you ask it to remember. Optional Device memory, when enabled, automatically saves successful structural patterns (package, view ID, class and gesture), never visible text, clipboard content, screenshots or terminal commands.
Reads text and interface structure exposed by Android Accessibility. Vision-capable models can also receive an on-demand screenshot.
Passwords, payment details, recovery codes and private messages may appear on screen. Never ask Jarvis to expose or repeat secrets.
Android may block secure windows, protected media, banking screens or system dialogs. Jarvis cannot bypass those protections.
You can stop the service from the dashboard or notification and revoke Accessibility, overlay, microphone or battery access in Android settings.
Can copy or paste exact text and run cancellable Linux commands in the active ReDHawK AI project when Terminal Runner is enabled. Commands can change project files, so review their target.

Optional Live conversation and “Hey Jarvis” repeatedly activate Android speech recognition through the visible foreground service, can hold a partial wake lock for screen-off listening, and increase battery use. Recognition may run on-device or through your phone’s speech provider.
Only enable Jarvis if you understand its access. You are responsible for reviewing commands and results, especially before messages, purchases, account changes or deletion.
Android secure windows and controls that do not expose Accessibility information may remain unavailable.

Jarvis inspects the interface only while executing a command. Live conversation and “Hey Jarvis” repeatedly use Android speech recognition until disabled; no raw audio is stored by ReDHawK Code. Vision screenshots remain in temporary cache, at most the newest three.
